subject.title: feat: add semantic Windows exec approval prompts

question: Should Windows approvals adopt agent-supplied semantic previews as a primary decision aid, provided the exact command remains visible and host policy/sandbox enforcement stays authoritative?
rationale: This changes the operator-facing consent boundary rather than only internal text formatting; maintainers must confirm that the intended trust and disclosure model is acceptable.

options.title: Approve the semantic-preview direction
options.body: Keep the preview as clearly labeled context, require simultaneous exact-command visibility, and land only after the localized identity fix and native Windows proof.

options.title: Retain technical-command-first approvals
options.body: Keep the current primary decision surface and limit this work to optional supplementary explanatory text after a separate UX/security design decision.

recommendation.title: Approve the semantic-preview direction
recommendation.body: Keep the preview as clearly labeled context, require simultaneous exact-command visibility, and land only after the localized identity fix and native Windows proof.
